releases.notes:
### Added

- **An immersive skin menu**
> In a world, opening the skin menu no longer covers the screen: the camera steps back in front of your character and the menu floats around them, tilted toward you. Your real player is the one you dress. They play the menu's poses (standing, walking, sitting on a block) and the little move when you pick a skin, and a click on an armour piece hides it, right on your character. The cape menu and the cape editor float the same way and turn your character round so you see the cape: the cape you point at or are editing is the one they wear, on elytra wings too in the Elytra tab. Going from the skin menu to the cape menu and back fades one into the other while the camera glides, and the dialogs (Delete, Rename, Nickname, Settings and the rest) open flat over the tilted menu. Near a wall the camera keeps its distance and opens a round window through the blocks between it and you, also with an Iris or Oculus shader pack. Outside a world the menus are as before. Turn it off with Immersive skin menu in Quick Skin's settings (Client tab). It works on every Minecraft version Quick Skin supports.

- **Other players see your poses**
> While you are in the immersive skin menu, other players with Quick Skin 5.0.0 see your character take the menu's pose, facing the way it faces there, and the pose ends when you close the menu. It needs Quick Skin 5.0.0 on the server too; a server turns it off with `allowImmersivePoses` in `quickskin-server.json`. Nothing you wear or save changes: it is only how your character is drawn.

### Changed

- **Skins are opaque with Ears**
> The Ears mod keeps its extra data (ears, tail, wings and the rest) in the transparency of a skin's body, where Minecraft draws a skin opaque. Quick Skin showed those parts half see-through. With Ears installed, Quick Skin now always shows skins opaque there, its "Show transparent parts of skins as opaque" setting stays ticked and says why, and a skin you import keeps that data in its file. Your own choice for that setting comes back if you remove Ears.

### Fixes

- **No more crash with Touch'n Motion when you hide your chestplate**
> On Minecraft 1.20.1 and 1.21.1, with Touch'n Motion and a Fresh Animations player pack, hiding your chestplate in the skin menu closed the game with "Pose stack not empty" as soon as you walked in third person. A hidden piece now leaves its layer drawing nothing instead of cutting that layer short, so what other mods do around it stays whole.

- **Hiding armour from the skin menu works on Fabric 1.20.1**
> On Fabric 1.20.1 a click on an armour piece of the skin menu's model did nothing; it now hides the piece, as it did on Forge.

- **An elytra in an accessory slot hides your cape**
> With an elytra in a Curios or Trinkets slot, your Quick Skin cape stayed on your back under the wings. It now hides while the elytra is worn there and comes back when you take it off, as with an elytra in the chest slot.

- **A CPM model no longer keeps the last skin's cape**
> In the skin menu, picking a CPM model right after a skin with a cape left that cape on the menu's model until you opened the menu again. The model now shows without it, as it is worn.

- **A CPM model picked on the title screen shows as the model**
> In the skin menu before you join a world, a CPM model picked a few seconds after opening the menu showed its icon instead of the model for the rest of the visit. It now shows the model.

### Added

- **CPM models show as models in every menu**
> With Customizable Player Models installed, your CPM model is now drawn as the model itself before you join a world: on the title screen's player, on the skin menu's big model when you pick a model there, and in the cape menu and the cape editor. Until now those showed your skin, or the model's icon, until you were in a world. The skin list and the favourites fan show a picture of each model made from the model itself, in the list's own style, instead of the icon saved in its file. It works on every Minecraft version Quick Skin supports, 26.3 included; with a CPM build too old to draw a model outside a world, the menus keep showing your skin or the model's icon.

- **JPG images as capes**
> The cape menu now takes JPG images too, dropped on it or picked from the file dialog, next to PNG, WebP and GIF. A JPG opens in the cape editor like any other picture, where you place it on the cape, and a photo taken with a phone opens the right way up. Skins saved as `.jpeg` are accepted as well; until now only `.jpg` was.

- **Big pictures as capes**
> A picture larger than 4096 pixels per side, such as a camera's photo or a long WebP, is now made smaller as it opens in the cape editor instead of being refused. PNG and JPG go up to 16384 pixels per side and 64 megapixels (32 for a progressive JPG); a WebP can have any shape up to 16 megapixels. A picture over that now says it is too big, or its size and the limit, instead of that it can't be opened as an image.

### Changed

- **Brighter player previews**
> Your player on the title screen, in the pause menu, in the skin and cape menus and in the corner preview is now lit from the front instead of with the inventory's dim light: the side facing you keeps all its colour and the rest most of it, so dark skins no longer look like a black shape.

### Fixes

- **A CPM model no longer ends up twisted after you pick a look**
> With Customizable Player Models on Minecraft 1.21.1 and older, picking a skin or a model in the skin menu inside a world could leave your character bent out of shape, in the menu and in the world, until you restarted the game. The little move the menu's model makes when you pick a look no longer stays on the player.

- **The cape menu shows the skin you opened it for**
> Right-click a skin and pick Assign cape or Change cape, and the cape menu's model now wears that skin. In a world it showed the skin you were wearing, which could be another one.

- **A cape on an invisible player**
> A player with the Invisibility effect no longer shows their Quick Skin cape floating in the air: the cape hides with the player, as a Minecraft cape does. Armour and elytra still show, as they do in Minecraft.

- **No more crash in third person with Touch'n Motion**
> With Touch'n Motion and an Entity Model Features player animation pack, wearing a Quick Skin cape closed the game with "Pose stack not empty" as soon as your player was drawn, for example in third person. Quick Skin now draws its cape without cutting Minecraft's own cape layer short, so what other mods do around that layer stays whole.

- **The cape preview stays turned to the cape**
> On Minecraft 1.20.1, dragging the player in the cape menu or in the cape editor turned it, and letting go left it facing you with the cape out of sight. That preview no longer turns: it always shows the player from behind, where the cape is.

- **A Quick Skin error can no longer keep a world from loading**
> What Quick Skin does when you enter, respawn in or leave a world is now kept apart from the game's own work: if it ever fails, the failure goes to the log and the world loads anyway. On Forge 1.20.1 such a failure left the game on "Joining world..." forever with no error screen, or sent you back to the menu with "Invalid player data".

- **The game no longer stops at startup over one unreadable file**

The skin list and the favourites fan show a picture of each model made from the model itself, in the list's own style, instead of the icon saved in its file. > The cape menu now takes JPG images too, dropped on it or picked from the file dialog, next to PNG, WebP and GIF. > A picture larger than 4096 pixels per side, such as a camera's photo or a long WebP, is now made smaller as it opens in the cape editor instead of being refused. > A player with the Invisibility effect no longer shows their Quick Skin cape floating in the air: the cape hides with the player, as a Minecraft cape does. Armour and elytra still show, as they do in Minecraft.

- **The game no longer stops at startup over one unreadable file**

releases.notes:
### Added

- **A favourites fan**
> Bind the new Favourites Fan key in Quick Skin's settings (Client tab) or in Controls › Quick Skin, and one press fans your favourite skins and CPM models out as cards over the hotbar, in the skin menu's order. You keep walking while it is open: the mouse points at the cards instead of turning the camera, a click wears the card you point at, and the key again, Esc or a right click puts it away. The mouse wheel turns the page when you have more favourites than fit, and on a server with a skin-change cooldown the fan tells you how long is left.

- **Elytra with a cape of their own**
> The cape menu has Cape and Elytra tabs: in the Elytra tab, pick any cape for your elytra, keep them the same as your cape, or give them vanilla's elytra texture. In the Cape tab, right-click a cape to put it on your elytra. Other players with Quick Skin 4.1.0 see your elytra's own cape; players on older versions see your elytra wear your cape as before.

- **Every skin wears its own cape**
> Capes now belong to skins: each skin wears its own cape or none, and putting a skin on, from the skin menu or the favourites fan, puts its cape on. The cape menu picks the cape of the skin you are wearing; right-click any skin in the skin menu and pick Assign a cape... to choose another skin's. Its Elytra tab picks what the elytra wear with that skin (its cape, vanilla's elytra or another cape). A skin without a cape shows none at all, not even your Mojang cape, to you and to everyone else. # Changelog

## 4.0.0 (2026-10-31)

### Added

- **A new skin menu built around your player**
> The skin menu drops its panel: your player stands in the middle on a turntable you can drag to turn, with your skins in a column of face tiles on the left, the player search at the top and the Body (arm width), Skin Websites (Normal or HD), Cape and pose buttons around the model. Clicking a skin wears it at once, and a button beside the sort button switches the column between the compact grid and a list where every skin gets a card with a 3D bust, its arm model and its resolution.

- **Favourites, a delete mode and a right-click menu for skins**
> Mark skins and CPM models as favourites to keep them right after your own skin in every sort order. Right-click a skin to favourite, rename or delete it, or use the bin beside the view button to pick several skins and delete them together. Added, favourited and deleted skins now animate in the column.

- **Nicknames**
> Click the name above your player in the skin menu to pick a nickname, kept per launcher account. On a server with Quick Skin everyone sees it in chat, death and advancement messages and the tab list, players without Quick Skin included, and players with Quick Skin also see it above your head; join and leave messages show "Nickname (Account)", operators still see account names in the tab list, and commands keep using account names. Server owners can turn player nicknames off with `allowNicknames` in `config/quickskin-server.json`.

- **Hide pieces of your armour from everyone**
> The skin menu's and the pause menu's models now wear what you wear and hold. Hover a piece of armour or an elytra on the skin menu's model to see through it, and click it to hide it from every other player, players without Quick Skin included; the piece stays worn and still protects you, and hidden pieces lie on the floor around the turntable, where a click puts them back on. The choice is kept per launcher account, and server owners can turn it off with `allowHiddenArmor` in `config/quickskin-server.json`, for example for PvP.

- **Admin tools for nicknames and skins**
> Operators can give players nicknames with `/quickskin nickname set`, hand out a different name to each player from `config/quickskin-nicknames.txt` with `random`, and take them back, clear or lock them with `reset`, `clear`, `lock` and `unlock`. They can also give players a skin for now, which other Quick Skin players see over the player's own skin until it is taken back, from the Player skins panel in the Server tab of the settings or with `/quickskin skin set|copy|random|shuffle|reset`; PNG skins put in `config/quickskin-skins/` join the server's skin pool (`/quickskin skin pool list|add|remove|reload`). Made for games where nobody should know who is who.

- **A reworked cape menu**
> Capes are now cards in sections (Favourites, My Capes, then the built-in capes by where they come from) under a heading that stays pinned while you scroll, with an import tile at the end of My Capes that you can click or drop files on. A large player on the right wears whichever cape is under the mouse, with the worn cape's animation speed under it; a click wears a cape, a right click marks it as a favourite or, for your own capes, edits or deletes it, and the mouse wheel scrolls the list wherever the mouse is.

- **A redesigned cape editor**
> The cape editor has a new layout with a 3D preview that shows the cape either as a cape or on elytra, Resolution, Position (Center, Snap, Mirror) and Opaque fill controls beside the canvas, and a zoom panel under it. It opens showing only the Front guide; a legend in the canvas corner turns the Cape Back and Elytra guides on and off, and hidden faces are dimmed.

- **Edit animated capes on a timeline**

# Changelog

## 3.1.1 (2026-10-11)

### Added

- **Compact Change Skin button**
> The new "Compact Change Skin Button" setting, in the Client tab, shows the Change Skin button of the title screen and the pause menu as a small Quick Skin icon, the same size as the language and accessibility buttons. The player preview and its buttons move to stand right above it. It is off by default and changes nothing when Essential is installed.
> *@Suelvys thx for the idea!*

- **Players without Quick Skin can see your new account skin**
> Server owners can turn on `shareAccountSkinWithVanillaClients` in `config/quickskin-server.json` (off by default). On an online-mode server, when you upload a skin to your Mojang account with the Upload to Mojang button, players who don't have Quick Skin see the new skin within a minute or two instead of only after you rejoin. Capes, HD skins and CPM models are still only visible to players with Quick Skin.

- **Upload limit for servers**
> Server owners can choose the biggest skin or cape that is synced to other players with `maxTextureUploadKilobytes` in `config/quickskin-server.json` (64 to 16384 KiB, 16384 by default). A skin or cape over the limit stays on your own screen, a chat message tells you why, and the rest of your appearance still syncs. Players on Quick Skin 3.1.0 or older should update before a server lowers the limit.

### Fixes

- **No more crash at launch with loading-screen mods**
> The game no longer crashes on startup ("No model for layer minecraft:player#main") when a mod that removes the loading screen, like Remove Reloading Screen, is installed. The title screen's player preview simply shows up once the game has finished loading.
> *@Llohgun thx for reporting it!*

- **The Change Skin button lines up with Quit Game on NeoForge**
> On NeoForge, the title screen's Change Skin button, together with the player preview above it, sat a few pixels higher than the Options and Quit Game row. It now sits on that row.
> *@Suelvys thx for reporting it!*

- **Importing skins on Android**
> On Android launchers, Import Skin now opens a file browser inside the game instead of doing nothing. If your file isn't listed, copy it into the game folder; the "Game folder" button takes you there.
> *@GIGTY thx for reporting it!*

- **No more disconnects from big skins on servers with Quick Skin 2.x**
> On a server that still runs Quick Skin 2.x, another player's large skin or GIF cape no longer disconnects you with "ByteArray with size ... is bigger than allowed 32768".

- **Smooth title-screen panorama with Very Many Players**
> With Very Many Players installed, the main menu's panorama turned in visible steps once the computer had been on for a few days, and jumped every few hours. It turns smoothly again.

- **Better performance with many capes around**
> Every visible Quick Skin cape now takes less work per frame, which helps on servers with lots of caped players.

- **The cape menu message no longer covers the buttons**
> The "Imported cape" and "Cape deleted" messages of the cape menu now show above the buttons instead of on top of Remove Cape.

- **More translations**
> The newest texts (skin search errors, the cape editor and the preview settings) are now translated into every language instead of showing up in English.

## 3.1.0 (2026-10-05)

### Added

- **FancyMenu compatibility**
> You can now hide, move and resize the player preview of the title screen and the pause menu from FancyMenu's layout editor. Hiding it also hides its rotate and animation buttons.
> *@Lappland and @EC thx for the idea!*

- **Option to hide the player preview in the menus**
> The new "Show Title Screen Preview" and "Show Pause Menu Preview" settings, in the Client tab, turn off the big player model on the title screen or on the pause menu. The Change Skin button stays.
> *@Lappland and @EC thx for the idea!*

- **Edit button for capes made with the cape editor**
